what: Second adversarial review of the presence build: the same five lenses, told what round 1 fixed (presence-round1.json), checking each fix and looking for regressions. Reviewed at commits dd459c6..64a38a1; fixed in 64a38a1, b1916a8 and the commit that adds this record.

verified_ok: Rebuilt at HEAD dd459c6 (python3 build-data.py && node build.js; working tree stayed clean); test/shots.js passed at 1280 and 390 px, light and dark, and wrote dist/preview.html, which I drove with Playwright (scripts in scratchpad/review2/claims/).

Round-1 fixes that hold: Punch and Clap show the subsonic 'thump' callout with no blast chart; Silent strike hides the knuckle-temperature tile and the 'thunderclap' sentence; the throw's 'passenger' hazard (launch peak g against the ASTM ramp, drag against 1.5 g) shows on the Throw tab; least disruptive never goes above the courtesy ceiling (tank, car, person); the 'whole planet' reach label; Lift with Gentle hold ('none needed', math line explains the spread push); the Walk canon sentence now runs an all-out stomp at the current strength and uses the in-step case for 'Both together'; the glass is judged on side-to-side shaking (chart curve and verdict); WALK.SOFT 0.51 in the math and cards; the Stomp tab's shaking uses the stamp's effective mass; '1 g up and down: loose things hop (whether people stumble ... is untested)'; Krakatoa growth text stops at 'about 0.3% ... unnoticeable'; instant growth caps the launch by the ground's bearing ('He still leaves the ground at 0.898 m/s and rises about 4.1 cm'); runaway gravity labelled weak-field, 'reaches 1 only at his own event horizon'; Wrestle→Throw uses the supersonic blast rule; the duo 'none' branch prints 'Courtesy ceiling: none' instead of 10⁻¹²%.

Growth numbers on the Weight tab match research/final-presence.json: Chicxulub 4,680 t (1,600×), mix 10.4 m at 41,800 kg/m³, pure size 35.3 m, pure density 1.6 × 10⁶ kg/m³; one solar second 1.4 million×, mix 32.3 m at 1.3 × 10⁶, pure size 342 m, pure density 1.5 × 10⁹; Krakatoa 9.35 kg. Gradual Chicxulub shortest harmless time 86.3 s (research: about 1½ min); instant timescale = new height ÷ 1,540 m/s (2.1, 6.7 and 23 ms); runaway ratio about 6 × 10⁻¹⁶ (research 5 × 10⁻¹⁶ mix) and gravity share 3 × 10⁻²⁴ at canon; 0.3 × (2 − s/3) reproduces 0.6/0.55/0.5 r_s/R.
Krakatoa and Chicxulub what-if rows carry their 'Claimed' and 'Disputed' statuses with the published ranges.

Gradual growth text (0.25 m/s OSHA head speed, 100 Pa at 2 m, 'borrowed from robot safety, not tested') and instant growth wording ('our choice of timescale', 'grows from his soles (our choice; an open question for the owners)') are labelled as estimates and choices.

Ground-shaking verdict, tiles and chart agree at the listener distance for Rex, Ollie and Both on concrete, sand, soft clay, granite and ice (ice: 'the lab doesn’t model ground shaking'); 'Both' chart main line, distances and verdict all use the doubled in-step case.

Walk tab thresholds match the research: 0.3 mm/s feel (BS 5228-2), 1 mm/s one jolt (Caltrans transient), 7.6 mm/s walk past and 12.7 mm/s one event (Caltrans/USBM RI 8507), 1 g cap g·T/2π (58 mm/s at 27 Hz, 100 mm/s at 16 Hz), rattle 1 mm/s labelled our estimate; elephant body-mass match (Larramendi 2016 cow 3.0 t) and 'no sharp impulses ... surprisingly faint' (Steinmann 2025) are as sourced.
134 dB = 100 Pa (20·log10(100/20 µPa) = 134.0); the air-hazard name and the card cite USBM RI 8485's safe maximum correctly; Kinney–Graham 100 Pa radius for 0.94 kg TNT is 820 m as the page says.

Throw person: launch felt g, the ASTM F2291 −Gx ramp (2 g at 0.2 s to 1.5 g held, 'keeping 2 g there is our estimate'), Eiband 11 g at 1.06 s, and 'like falling 3.47 m' landing all compute consistently; Safe passenger shows 'Safe passenger, but air drag 3.4 g' at 80 m/s on the Throw tab.

Presets order and wording on the default car throw ('At this effort it also rattles windows ... from where it lands' under least disruptive); the not-so-heroic presets that can't be reached say 'Even all-out, this move doesn’t ...' with correct verb forms (rattle, shake, break, blast).

Other moves (jump, stomp, punch, clap, sprint, pull) showed no false 'unreachable' goal, no crash and no 'none' ceiling with all-out hazards across concrete, granite and sand, comic ground on and off, both muscle modes, 10^6-10^10 kg and unlimited strength (engine scan).

Two-player Arm wrestle: ceiling at the 15.1 kN table limit (6.14 t effort, arm 25%) is consistent; Collide's thump rule (35 ms hit) matches the Collide tab; Catch counts palm crush and the person's throw and catch g when Safe passenger is off.

findings.title: Throw: the saturation stop makes heavy throws claim 'even all-out he can't' reach the goal when all-out does, and crashes the tab on granite
findings.location: src/engine.js RESTRAINT.search (the `same` stop) + plan().same; src/app.html resolveEffort ('least' branch: EFF_HAZ[ce.by].what with ce.by null)
findings.evidence: Default comic mode and concrete, Throw tab, object M1A2 Abrams tank, strength 100,000 t (logKg 8). The page says: 'The tank flies 10.8 m.' / 'Even all-out he can’t land the tank 30 m away, and past 0.29% (lifting 294 t) the ground under his feet gives way.' Engine at the same settings, all-out: v 43.7 m/s, range 188 m. Semi at 10,000 t: 'Even all-out he can’t land the semi 30 m away' while all-out throws it 61.1 m. Why: comic mode holds back to the footing, so launch speed is flat over half a decade (tank: 9.79 m/s at both 1e6 and 3e6 kg; granite: 8.40 m/s at 3e5 and 1e6), `same()` declares the move saturated, and the goal and every hazard search return 'never'. On granite (tank, 100,000 t or more; also soft clay with Comic ground from 10,000 t) the hazards are real at all-out, ceiling() returns by:null and the tab shows 'Calculation failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'what')' with a console TypeError. My engine scan of the throw (4 surfaces x comic ground x 2 modes x 8 strengths x 8 objects, script scratchpad/review2/claims/scan_sat.js) found 63 settings where the goal is falsely called unreachable, 13 where the page crashes, and the same 13 where 'Courtesy ceiling: none ... even all-out' is shown although all-out has boom, plaster, ground or crush hazards. Other moves: none found.
findings.expected: A plateau caused by the footing hold-back, or by switching between muscle models, is not saturation: more effort still throws farther (tank 9.79 -> 43.7 m/s). The goal search should find the 30 m throw, and the ceiling should name the hazard that all-out actually trips.
findings.fix: Only stop when the result is the same at the top of the range too (e.g. also compare with run(hi)), or require the speed to stay flat over a full decade and to equal the all-out speed. In resolveEffort, guard `ce.by` null (treat it as no ceiling and fall back to all-out). Add a test: tank and semi on concrete and granite at 1e7-1e10 kg, goal reached iff all-out reaches it.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD d048813. Note: the working tree changed while I was reviewing, so every run below uses a HEAD snapshot (git show HEAD:… into scratchpad/review2/verify_claims/head/). Page, Throw, tank, logKg 8, concrete, least disruptive: 'The tank flies 10.8 m.' / 'Even all-out he can’t land the tank 30 m away, and past 0.29% (lifting 294 t) the ground under his feet gives way.' The same settings at All-out: 'The tank flies 188 m.' For the semi at logKg 7 the page says 'Even all-out he can’t land the semi 30 m away', but all-out throws it 61.1 m. On granite (tank, logKg 8) the bay shows 'Calculation failed: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'what')' and the console logs a TypeError. Engine (f1e.js): the tank's launch speed is 9.79177 m/s at both 9.51e5 and 3.01e6 kg, two grid points half a decade apart, so same() stops the goal search; all-out gives 43.67 m/s and goal=true. On granite, ceiling() returns by:null although the crush hazard is true at all-out, and resolveEffort then reads EFF_HAZ[null].what. The crash is common: with Comic ground and Gentle hold, the loco at logKg 8.5 and the cc177, b777 and Liberty at logKg 9 all crash the Throw tab (f24p.js). Proposed fix tested on an engine copy (f1fix.js): requiring the plateau speed to equal the all-out speed finds the goal (tank 1.38e8 N, semi 4.28e7 N, granite tank 7.45e7 N) and finds granite's crush ceiling.
verdict.better_fix: engine.js plan(): `const eq = (a, b) => a > 0 && isFinite(a) && Math.abs(b - a) <= 1e-6 * a; const same = (u0, u1) => { const a = M.speed(at(u0)), b = M.speed(at(u1)); return eq(a, b) && eq(a, M.speed(at(hi))); };` This stops only on a plateau that has already reached the all-out result. In app.html resolveEffort's 'least' branch, guard a null ce.by: `if (!ce.by) { out.use = undefined; out.why = 'Nothing this move does harms anyone nearby, so he can go all-out.'; return out; }`. Add a test: tank and semi on concrete and granite, with and without comic ground and gentle hold, at 1e7–1e10 kg. The goal must be reached exactly when all-out reaches it, and ceiling().by must be non-null whenever a hazard holds at all-out.

outcome.change: Saturation now also requires the all-out run to match (a held-back plateau isn't the top); resolveEffort guards a ceiling with no hazard. New test: nothing reported as never happens all-out (tank, semi, loco, jump on ice and concrete); it fails on the old rule in all six cases.

findings.title: Two-player readout says 'Nothing in this test can harm anything nearby' while 3-tonne bodies slide through the 5 m zone at 9-156 m/s
findings.location: src/app.html duoHarm ('wrestle' shove: only supersonic counts; 'collide': only blast; 'catch': thrower recoil not counted) and duoEffortBox readout
findings.evidence: Wrestle, move Shove, default 100 t: verdict 'Ollie flies back at 14.4 m/s and slides 17.5 m, well out of the ring. Rex recoils at 14.5 m/s.' (630 kJ, 150 g TNT); readout 'All-out: no cap needed. Nothing in this test can harm anything nearby, so they go all-out.' At 10,000 t (logKg 7): 'Ollie flies back at 156 m/s and slides 857 m ... Rex recoils at 156 m/s' (73.6 MJ) with the same readout. At unlimited strength the least-disruptive cap stops only at 'someone flies off faster than sound', so both slide 1.6 km at 340 m/s. Collide default: 'Rex is knocked back at 8.97 m/s and the two slide 6.97 m before they stop' + 'Nothing in this test can harm anything nearby'. Catch, car fastball, 1,000,000 t, Gentle hold, least disruptive: 'Throwing it shoves Rex back at 151 m/s and slides about 838 m' under 'The hardest both can go while nothing around them breaks.' People and buildings are taken to be 5 m away (state.near).
findings.expected: A 3 t body moving at 9-156 m/s, sliding farther than the 5 m 'near' distance, is a harm to people and buildings there (a 52 km/h car crash at the default). The readout cannot claim nothing nearby can be harmed.
findings.fix: Count a body (Rex, Ollie, or the thrown partner) that slides or is knocked past state.near at more than walking speed as harm in duoHarm for shove, collide and catch (thrower recoil); otherwise reword to 'Nothing the lab checks here (table, object, sonic boom, air blast) is harmed' and say the bodies' own slide is not counted.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD (f2.js, output in duo_head.out). Wrestle > Shove at the default dial: 'Ollie flies back at 14.4 m/s and slides 17.5 m, well out of the ring. Rex recoils at 14.5 m/s.' Tiles: 'Ollie slides 17.5 m', 'Rex slides 17.6 m', 630 kJ. The readout says 'All-out: no cap needed. Nothing in this test can harm anything nearby, so they go all-out.' At logKg 7 both slide 857–867 m at 156 m/s (73.6 MJ) under the same readout. Collide default: 'Rex is knocked back at 8.97 m/s and the two slide 6.97 m' with the same 'Nothing ... can harm' line. Catch, car, Fastball, logKg 9, Gentle hold: Ollie's feet slide 440 m. Code: duoHarm('wrestle'/'shove') returns harm only when max(vA, vB) >= K.a0, collide counts only the blast, and P.shove already returns slideA/slideB. A 3-tonne body crossing the 5 m 'near' line at 52 km/h or more would hit anyone standing there, so the claim is false.
verdict.better_fix: In duoHarm, shove: `const slide = Math.max(r.slideA || 0, r.slideB || 0); if (slide > near && Math.max(r.vA || 0, r.vB || 0) > 1.5) return 'someone is shoved ' + fmtDist(slide) + ', past people ' + fmtDist(near) + ' away';` Do the same for collide (the knock-back distance, r.after) and for catch (the thrower's recoil and the catcher's slide). If that is not done, reword the readout to 'Nothing the lab checks here (table, object, sonic boom, air blast) is harmed; the two bodies’ own slide is not counted.'

outcome.change: duoHarm counts a body sliding past the nearest people (shove, collide, the catch thrower's recoil).

findings.title: Hazards are tested only at exactly 5 m, but the page says 'within 5 m', so the ceiling and 'none' lines contradict their own reach figures
findings.location: src/app.html effortFields label 'People and buildings within (m)'; effortReadout ('within ' + near, 'harms anyone within'); engine HAZARDS test ppvAt(..., o.near)
findings.evidence: Stomp, default 100 t, concrete, preset Courtesy ceiling: 'Plaster may crack within 5 m from 68% (lifting 61 t); now out to 1.76 m.' (engine: 22 mm/s at 1 m, 12.7 mm/s at 1.76 m). Stomp on loose sand, opening view (least disruptive): 'Plaster may crack within 5 m from 0.6% (lifting 540 kg); now out to 1.14 m.' Stomp on loose sand at record-human strength (511 kg), All-out: 'Courtesy ceiling: none. Nothing this move does harms anyone within 5 m, even all-out.' and 'None of the hazards ... (ground shaking that may crack plaster ...) can happen', while the engine gives 50.7 mm/s at 1 m and 12.7 mm/s out to 4.82 m.
findings.expected: Either the hazard covers everything closer than the distance (then plaster cracking at 1.14-4.82 m is a hazard), or the copy must say the nearest people and buildings are 5 m away.
findings.fix: Relabel the input 'Nearest people and buildings (m)', and write 'at 5 m' / '5 m or more away' in the hazard list, the ceiling line and the 'none' line; or test the hazards at RMIN (1 m) up to near.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD. Stomp, default, Courtesy ceiling: 'Plaster may crack within 5 m from 68% (lifting 61 t); now out to 1.76 m.' At the 5.6% effort shown, plaster-cracking shaking already reaches 1.76 m, which is inside 5 m. The 'from 68%' onset is where it reaches exactly 5 m. Stomp on loose sand at 511 kg, All-out: 'Courtesy ceiling: none. Nothing this move does harms anyone within 5 m, even all-out.' Engine (f3e.js) gives 50.7 mm/s at 1 m, 16.8 at 3 m and 12.4 at 5 m, with the plaster reach (12.7 mm/s) at 4.82 m. The input is labelled 'PEOPLE AND BUILDINGS WITHIN (M)', but HAZARDS tests ppvAt(..., o.near) only at that one distance.
verdict.better_fix: Relabel the input 'Nearest people and buildings (m)'. In effortReadout use '… harms anyone ' + fmtDist(near) + ' or more away' in place of 'within', and in the hazard list use EFF_HAZ name + ' ' + fmtDist(near) + ' away from …' in place of 'within 5 m from'. The alternative is to test the hazards at VIB.RMIN instead of near.

outcome.change: Field relabelled 'Nearest people and buildings (m)'; readout says 'at 5 m' and '5 m or more away'.

findings.title: Presets and 'At this effort it also...' state upper-bound blast effects as fact ('blasts houses 5 m away flat'), against the page's own upper-bound label and the source's caveat
findings.location: src/app.html PRESET_WHAT and effortReadout ('At this effort it also ...'); preset labels 'Crack the plaster next door', 'Flatten the houses next door', 'Level a block'; engine PRESETS (DP_HOUSES 26.8 kPa)
findings.evidence: Punch, 10,000 t (logKg 7), preset Rattle the windows: verdict 'His fist reaches 340 m/s. Every punch cracks like a whip, only louder.'; readout 'The least effort that rattles windows ...' then 'At this effort it also blasts houses 5 m away flat.' and 'Air blast ... now out to 820 m from him'. The energy is 3.92 MJ (0.94 kg TNT); Kinney–Graham gives 26.8 kPa at 5.13 m only if all of it becomes blast. The bay's own blast chart says 'Upper bound: real moves couple far less energy into air than explosives do', and the card says the radii 'are upper bounds'. research/final-environment.json blast_residential_collapse notes: 'Derived from 1 kt (nuclear, long-duration) blast; short-duration blasts from small charges need higher peak pressure for the same damage.' The 'plaster' preset uses 12.7 mm/s, which the card itself calls a safe limit 'below which cracks are very unlikely' (Siskind: 5% chance at 13 mm/s), yet the preset is labelled 'Crack the plaster next door'. The lowest preset ('Rattle the windows') here already flattens houses, so the 'rising scales' are one step.
findings.expected: Blast-based preset effects worded as upper bounds ('could blast houses flat, as an upper bound'), house collapse from a sub-kilogram charge not stated as fact, and the plaster preset worded as 'risks cracking plaster'.
findings.fix: Add 'up to' / 'could' to PRESET_WHAT's windows, houses and block text and to the 'At this effort it also' line for blast items, with a short note that blasts assume all the energy goes into the air; rename the preset 'Risk cracking the plaster next door'; make the punch verdict past Mach 1 say what the readout says (or say the blast is an upper bound).

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD. Punch, logKg 7, preset Rattle the windows: the readout says 'At this effort it also blasts houses 5 m away flat.' and 'Air blast … now out to 820 m from him'. The same bay's chart says 'Damage radius if all of that energy went into the air as a blast … Upper bound: real moves couple far less energy into air than explosives do.' The assumption card also says the radii 'are upper bounds'. 820 m checks out against the far-field Kinney–Graham law ΔP/P0 ≈ 0.827/Z with 0.94 kg TNT, so the number is right but it is an upper bound stated as fact. The research note on blast_residential_collapse says the 26.8 kPa level comes from 1 kt nuclear long-duration blasts and that small charges need more pressure. The preset name 'Crack the plaster next door' also claims more than its own readout text ('plaster may crack') and the card's 'safe limit' wording for 12.7 mm/s.
verdict.better_fix: PRESET_WHAT.windows/houses/block: 'could break windows …' / 'could flatten houses …, as an upper bound (if all its energy became blast)'. Apply the same 'could … (upper bound)' wording to blast items in the 'At this effort it also' line. Rename the preset 'Risk cracking the plaster next door'.

outcome.change: Window, house and block presets say 'could' and give the upper-bound basis (all energy into the air; a long nuclear blast for houses).

findings.title: Show-the-math and tiles say the push is a share of 'the dial's force' / 'full strength' when it is a share of the effort; one verdict blames strength for an effort cap
findings.location: src/app.html bayJump math (line ~1407), bayThrow math (line ~1327) and the 'His throwing push' tile and can't-throw verdict (lines ~1206-1211)
findings.evidence: Jump, default, least disruptive: dial 'Lifts 90.7 t / 890 kN of force'; math 'Legs push his body (2,920 kg) up ... with 149 kN (66% of the dial’s force, constant)'. 66% of 890 kN is 587 kN; 149 kN is 66% of the 23 t effort. Throw default: 'Drive: 261 kN (52% of full strength per hand, capped at his full strength ...)'; 261 kN is 29% of his full strength. Throw, locomotive, 100,000 t, Comic ground, preset Courtesy ceiling: verdict 'Rex can hold it, but can’t throw it at any angle: his throwing push (610.3 kN) is less than the weight ... (1.816 MN)' beside tiles 'His full strength 980.7 MN' and 'His throwing push 610.3 kN, 17% of full strength per hand'.
findings.expected: Under effort the drive is a share of the strength used (the effort), and a throw blocked by the effort cap is not a strength limit.
findings.fix: Use 'of the strength he uses' (or 'of his effort') when c.use < c.F, show the effort in the 'His full strength' tile, and make the verdict say 'at this effort'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD. Jump, least disruptive (effort 23 t): 'Legs push … with 149 kN (66% of the dial’s force, constant)'. 0.66 × 23 t × g = 149 kN, while 66% of the 100-short-ton dial would be 587 kN. Throw default (effort 26.6 t): 'Drive: 261 kN (52% of full strength per hand, capped at his full strength …)'. 261 kN is 100% of the effort and 29% of his strength. Throw, loco, logKg 8, Comic ground, Courtesy ceiling (0.19%): the verdict 'can’t throw it at any angle: his throwing push (610.3 kN) is less than …' blames his strength for what is the effort cap. driveStrength(ctx) = min(F, use) confirms the share is of the effort.
verdict.better_fix: Pass the strength used to the text: `const ofWhat = c.use != null && c.use < c.F ? 'of the strength he uses' : 'of the dial’s force'` (and the same for 'full strength'). Add an 'Effort used' tile next to 'His full strength'. When c.use < c.F, add 'at this effort' to the can’t-throw verdict.

outcome.change: Jump and Throw math, the throw tile and the can't-throw verdict name the strength he uses when the effort is below the dial.

findings.title: Catch with Safe passenger: air drag on the thrown person is not counted, contradicting the Throw tab's rule
findings.location: src/app.html catchPassengerG (returns null when state.safePassenger) and duoHarm('catch')
findings.evidence: Rex + Ollie > Catch, object 'A person', Fastball, Safe passenger on, default strength: 'Rex fires the person at 78.2 m/s'; readout 'All-out: no cap needed. Nothing in this test can harm anything nearby' and chip 'Safe passenger: throw and catch spread through them'. Engine PASSENGER.dragG(person, 78.2) = 3.26 g, above noHarm(1) = 1.5 g and noHarm(0.093 s) = 2 g. The Throw tab at 80.3 m/s with the same switch shows 'Safe passenger, but air drag 3.4 g' and '...past the 1.5 g rides allow for that long; Safe passenger covers only his push, not the air' and counts it as the passenger hazard. Without the switch the Catch tab never checks drag either.
findings.expected: The same rule on both tabs: drag on a flying person is real and counts against the ride limit.
findings.fix: In catchPassengerG check PASSENGER.dragG(o, L.aim.vL) against noHarm(1) whatever the switch, and show it as on the Throw tab.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD. Catch, A person, Fastball, Safe passenger on: 'Rex fires the person at 78.2 m/s … 93 ms later', and the readout says 'All-out: no cap needed. Nothing in this test can harm anything nearby'. Engine: PASSENGER.dragG(person, 78.2) = 3.26 g. That is above noHarm(1) = 1.5 g and also above noHarm(0.093 s) = 2 g, so the person is over the ride limit whichever limit is used. catchPassengerG returns null as soon as state.safePassenger is set, and it never checks drag even with the switch off. MOVES.throw.passenger on the Throw tab does count drag ('Safe passenger, but air drag 3.4 g … past the 1.5 g rides allow').
verdict.better_fix: In catchPassengerG, before the safePassenger early return: `const dG = P.PASSENGER.dragG(o, L.aim.vL); if (dG > P.PASSENGER.noHarm(1)) return { over: true, where: 'drag', n: dG, t: 1, limit: P.PASSENGER.noHarm(1) };`. Handle where==='drag' in duoHarm ('air drag presses the person harder than amusement rides allow') and add a matching chip.

outcome.change: Catch checks air drag on a thrown person whatever the switch, and shows it.

findings.title: Safe passenger switch promises 'no harmful g-force', and the landing caveat disappears from the readout when the switch is on
findings.location: src/app.html #sw-passenger label (line 355); effortReadout ('For a person this covers the launch only...' only when !state.safePassenger); 'Hazards checked' text
findings.evidence: Switch text: 'so they feel no harmful g-force. The landing stays real.' Throw a person, All-out, default strength, switch on: chip 'Safe passenger, but air drag 3.4 g' and '... past the 1.5 g rides allow'. findings.fix: Switch text: '...so his push puts no g-force on them; air drag in flight and the landing stay real.' Drop `&& !state.safePassenger` from the landing-note condition; add 'a thrown person past ride limits' to the 'Hazards checked' list.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD. The switch text says '…so they feel no harmful g-force. The landing stays real.' Throw a person, All-out, switch on: chip 'Safe passenger, but air drag 3.4 g' and the hazard 'Past ride limits for the person … happens now'. So the switch promises something the page itself contradicts. With the switch on, the readout drops the note 'For a person this covers the launch only… the lab doesn’t count it' (the condition is `&& !state.safePassenger`), though the landing is just as uncounted ('they hit the ground at 17 m/s … unless someone catches them'). Drop `&& !state.safePassenger` from the landing-note condition and make that note 'The landing is a fall unless someone catches them, and the lab doesn’t count it.' findings.title: Elephant tile says the elephant 'was measured walking past 50 m away' when the only measurement is at 20 m; the comparison has no estimate label
findings.location: src/app.html bayWalk elSub ('it was measured walking past ' + fmtDist(dE) + ' away')
findings.evidence: Walk, Rex, loose sand, listener 50 m: tile 'Compared with an elephant: 20× the elephant / both on sandy ground, as the elephant was; it was measured walking past 50 m away'. The note below says 'a wild African elephant measured 20 m from a seismometer, falling about as 1 ÷ distance'. research elephant_steinmann2025_walk_20m_ppv (derived, 20 m only) and elephant_anchor_ppv_vs_distance (estimate, 'Order of magnitude only'). The '30×/70×/700× the elephant' value carries no status label.

findings.fix: elSub: 'both on sandy ground, as the elephant was; measured at 20 m, scaled as 1 ÷ distance to ' + fmtDist(dE) + ' · estimate'.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on HEAD. Walk, loose sand, listener 50 m: the tile says '20× the elephant / both on sandy ground, as the elephant was; it was measured walking past 50 m away'. findings.evidence: The data fact blast_residential_collapse (26.8 kPa, Glasstone via Collins) carries the note: 'Derived from 1 kt (nuclear, long-duration) blast; short-duration blasts from small charges need higher peak pressure for the same damage.' review2/presets.js with the engine's blastRadius: 26.8 kPa at 5 m needs 0.865 kg TNT, while 6.9 kPa at 15 m (windows) needs 1.39 kg. - 26.8 kPa at 5 m needs 0.865 kg TNT;
- 6.9 kPa at 15 m needs 1.39 kg.

findings.evidence: review2/ux/s8-duo-drag.js presses 20% along each slider at 1280x900, drags to 80% in 21 mouse moves, then releases. Arm and Collide give the same result. `catch c-dist #c-dist inputs 1 ... final 1.92 expected about 5.95 same element false`. When the first input event fires, focus is still on BODY. The synchronous renderBay(true) therefore does not keep the controls: it replaces the bay and destroys the slider under the pointer. #o-effort-use works only because focus was already in the bay on the checkbox. Solo sliders render in requestAnimationFrame, after focus has moved, so they work (`solo throw ... inputs 21 ... same element true`). On the pre-round-1 build (0850eca, review2/ux/s8-old.js) the same Catch distance drag works: `#c-dist inputs 21 distinct values 21 ... final 5.96 ... same element true`. In review2/ux/s5-drag-timing.js the readout stays at 'Effort: 4% of his strength...' through the whole drag on Catch and Collide.

findings.fix: Keep the bay controls when the event came from inside the bay, not only when focus is already there. Two ways: pass the input's target to renderBay (`renderBay(true, e.target)`, keeping when `bay.contains(from)`), or call `e.target.focus()` before scheduleBaySlow(). Alternatively, make scheduleBaySlow's first render wait for requestAnimationFrame like scheduleBay.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on a rebuilt HEAD with v/drag.js and v/drag-arm.js (fresh page, 1280x900; press at 20%, 21 mouse moves to 80%, release). Catch #duo-effort-use: 1 input event, focus at the first input was BODY, final value 3.71 against about 4.65 expected, and the element was replaced. Catch #c-dist: 1 input, final 1.77 against about 5.95 expected, element replaced. Collide #duo-effort-use: final value 3.71, element replaced. Arm, fresh page: 1 input, focus BODY, element replaced. Solo Throw #effort-use: 22 inputs, 22 distinct values, final 4.29, same element. Cause: Chromium fires the slider's first input event inside the mousedown default action, before focus moves. scheduleBaySlow then calls renderBay(true) synchronously; `bay.contains(document.activeElement)` is false, so replaceChildren destroys the slider under the pointer, and focusId is null, so focus is not restored. `git log -S` shows the old scheduleBaySlow (a 180 ms debounce, keeping controls without the activeElement test) was replaced in 3454988, so this is a regression from that commit. Mouse drags on every two-player slider die after the first step; keyboard still works.
verdict.better_fix: Pass the event's source and keep the controls when it is inside the bay. In app.html: `function scheduleBaySlow(from) { if (slowTimer) { slowPending = true; return; } save(); renderBay(true, from); slowTimer = setTimeout(...) }`, and in the three handlers (:2193, :3366, :3376) call `scheduleBaySlow(e.target)`. In renderBay(keepControls, from): `const inBay = (n) => !!n && bay.contains(n); const old = keepControls && (inBay(document.activeElement) || inBay(from)) ? bay.querySelector(':scope > .bay-controls') : null;`. A simpler alternative: make scheduleBaySlow's first render wait one requestAnimationFrame, as scheduleBay does; focus has moved by then.
